summary: 47-year-old woman, not lactating, with 4 weeks of a red, warm, swollen right breast involving more than a third of the skin, peau d'orange, no fever, not improved after two courses of antibiotics. Inflammatory breast cancer until proven otherwise: urgent core biopsy of breast and skin, staging, neoadjuvant systemic therapy; no primary breast-conserving surgery.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Red swollen right breast not getting better with antibiotics
inputs.hpi: Four weeks of a red, heavy, swollen right breast. GP gave flucloxacillin then co-amoxiclav — no improvement. No fever, not breastfeeding (youngest child 9 years). Skin looks like orange peel. No lump felt.

exam.other: Right breast: diffuse erythema and oedema over more than a third of the breast, peau d'orange, warm, mildly tender, no fluctuance, no discrete mass. Firm right axillary nodes. Left breast normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected inflammatory breast cancer (right) — failed antibiotics, peau d'orange
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected inflammatory breast cancer (right): erythema and oedema >1/3 of the breast, peau d'orange, no fever, not lactating, failed two courses of antibiotics. Urgent mammography and ultrasound, core biopsy of breast and skin punch biopsy, staging CT; breast MDT for neoadjuvant systemic therapy.

mustNotMiss.note: Non-lactational "mastitis" not responding to antibiotics with peau d'orange is inflammatory breast cancer until proven otherwise.

mustExclude.note: NCCN: in inflammatory breast cancer, breast-conserving surgery and sentinel node biopsy are not recommended; surgery (modified radical mastectomy) follows neoadjuvant systemic therapy.
A third course of antibiotics delays diagnosis.

guideline.name: NCCN Guidelines — Breast Cancer (inflammatory breast cancer; breast cancer during pregnancy)
guideline.section: Inflammatory breast cancer: core biopsy of breast and skin, staging, neoadjuvant systemic therapy before modified radical mastectomy (breast conservation and sentinel node biopsy not recommended); breast cancer during pregnancy (no tamoxifen, no radiotherapy during pregnancy)
guideline.citation: National Comprehensive Cancer Network. NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer (current version at authoring).

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms (ABS / RCR, Department of Health)
guideline.section: Triple assessment (clinical examination, age-appropriate imaging, needle biopsy); imaging by age; nipple discharge; breast infection; breast pain
guideline.citation: Willett AM, Michell MJ, Lee MJR (eds). Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms. London: Department of Health / Association of Breast Surgery; 2010.

rationale: Must-not-miss breast case. Presentation words are "red, swollen breast", which an engine anchored on infection reads as mastitis. The surgeon codes the suspicion (C50.911) so the plan comes from the carcinoma protocol: tests that the protocol adapts to the inflammatory subtype.
